{{Quote|This is my decoy, my protection&hellip; my loyal bodyguard.|Padmé Amidala, to Boss Nass|<ref name="tpm" />}}
'''Sabé''' {{Pronounced|sɑ'beɪ}} was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] who served as a loyal [[Handmaiden/Legends|handmaiden]] to [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] during her reign as [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Monarch of Naboo]]. A native of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], Sabé was handpicked by [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Panaka]] of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] shortly after [[Coronation of Queen Amidala/Legends|Amidala's coronation]], due to her strong resemblance to the new queen. Along with the other handmaidens, Sabé was trained to serve as both an attendant and a [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]], and as the most important of her group, she was chosen to be the first in line to take the queen's place in [[Time/Legends|times]] of crisis, as a decoy. Together with Amidala, Sabé perfected her act as queen, learning to mimic the [[Monarchy/Legends|monarch]] accurately.

Sabé was required to step into the role during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. When the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] subjugated the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], the handmaiden donned one of the [[Padmé Amidala's wardrobe/Legends|queen's gowns]], while Amidala took Sabé's role, using concealed gestures and signals to communicate. Before they were taken into Federation custody, Sabé and her "retinue" were rescued by the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. In attempting to flee Naboo in the queen's [[J-type 327 Nubian royal starship/Legends|J-type 327 Nubian royal starship]], the group was forced to make a detour to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in order to repair the craft before journeying to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].

Once on Coruscant, Amidala attempted to reason with the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], and hoped to receive aid to help remove the Federation from Naboo. No such help came her way, however, and she was forced to take matters into her own hands. Sabé once again took on the role of the queen in an attempt to persuade the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] to help fight the Federation. Sabé's attempts failed, forcing the real Amidala to reveal her identity. The revelation impressed the Gungan leader, [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]], and he agreed to aid the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]]. Sabé then participated in the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], helping to defeat the Federation and free her [[Planet/Legends|planet]].

==Biography==
===Early career===
{{Quote|We will fight to protect our Queen.|Sabé to Padmé Naberrie, unaware of the latter's true identity|<ref name="QiD" />}}
[[File:QoD_Amidala_Handmaidens.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Sabé tending to Queen Amidala with the other handmaidens]]
Sabé was a [[Handmaiden/Legends|handmaiden]] in the service of [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="db" /> Amidala's head of security, [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Panaka]], handpicked Sabé and the other handmaidens following the [[Coronation of Queen Amidala/Legends|queen's coronation]] and had them trained in gymnastics, hand-to-hand combat and small arms handling. Despite their ability to serve as [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]], the handmaidens would also serve Amidala on a more personal level, tending to her [[Padmé Amidala's wardrobe/Legends|outfits]] and hairstyles.<ref name="ff">''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]''</ref>

Thinking ahead, Panaka devised a scheme to ensure the queen's safety in [[Time/Legends|times]] of crisis. Sabé, who bore a striking resemblance to Amidala, would adopt the role of the queen, while Amidala herself would pose as a handmaiden.<ref name="cpdb">{{DB|character|captainpanaka|Panaka, Captain}}</ref> The pair developed a set of signals they would use, while in disguise, to convey messages without arousing suspicion.<ref name="db" /> The queen would give her dialect lessons to aid her mimicry, but Sabé was always afraid that she would give away the ruse.<ref name="vd">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Though Sabé was usually first in line to play the role of "false queen," the other handmaidens could also fill the position if needs be.<ref name="ff" /> Due to her role as Amidala's decoy, Sabé was considered to be the most important of the queen's bodyguards. During her time as a handmaiden, Sabé became close friends with Amidala.<ref name="vd" />

[[File:PadmeAndSabe-QiD.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Sabé (right) and Padmé Amidala chasing a rogue training droid during the handmaidens' training]]
The handmaidens would constantly train at a secret compound set up by Panaka, located just outside [[Theed/Legends|Theed]]. There, they would hone their marksmanship under the captain's supervision. The training area included an obstacle course that the handmaidens had to navigate while constantly being harried by a floating [[Training droid/Legends|training droid]]. One [[Standard day/Legends|day]], the handmaidens were joined by a newcomer, named Padmé. [[Yané/Legends|Yané]] and [[Eirtaé/Legends|Eirtaé]] successfully completed the course that day, but [[Rabé/Legends|Rabé]] encountered some potentially fatal difficulties. Hit in the arm by the training [[Droid/Legends|droid's]] non-lethal [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] fire, Rabé returned fire, but even a direct hit was unable to down the droid. Padmé and Sabé also opened fire on the training device, to no avail. The duo quickly realized that something had gone amiss with the droid, and it pursued the fleeing Rabé to a nearby [[Water/Legends|waterfall]] while Yané went to alert the compound's droid control.<ref name="ff" />

While Rabé waited on the treacherous footing near the waterfall, Sabé, acting quickly, fired a cable at a nearby branch. Padmé swung from the cable, lashing out at the training droid and knocking it wildly off course. She then retrieved the injured Rabé from her dangerous position. When everyone was safe, Padmé revealed that she was in fact the queen, and in doing so she assured her handmaidens that their loyalty to her was returned in kind.<ref name="ff" />

===The occupation of Naboo===
{{Quote|I will not cooperate.|Sabé, as the queen|<ref name="tpm" />}}
[[File:SabeRabePadme-TPM.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Sabé, as the queen, and Padmé Amidala during the Invasion of Naboo]]
In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the forces of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] invaded Naboo as a part of their protest of the taxation of [[Hyperspace route/Legends|trade routes]]. Knowing that the queen would be in danger, Captain Panaka initiated his scheme to ensure the safety of Amidala. Sabé, due to her close resemblance to Amidala, took on her guise, while Amidala adopted handmaiden attire and used her birth name of "Padmé Naberrie".<ref name="tpm" /> Before the ruse could be completed, however, it was discovered that the [[Padmé Amidala's amulet|queen's amulet]] had gone missing. Sabé helped Amidala locate the object in a nearby meadow, allowing her costume to be completed.<ref name="tqa">''[[The Queen's Amulet]]''</ref>

Sabé was able to fool [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], although she did not have to keep up the ruse for long. Two [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], rescued "Amidala" and her retinue from the Federation's forces. Jinn, fearful that the Federation might harm the queen, insisted that she journey to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to put her case before the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. By giving advice to her decoy in her role as handmaiden, Amidala was able to acknowledge the decision without arousing the suspicion of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], and Sabé agreed with Jinn. As they left Naboo in the queen's unarmed [[J-type 327 Nubian royal starship/Legends|starship]], they sustained heavy fire from the Federation blockade that surrounded the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. Though they were able to safely make it out of the [[Naboo system/Legends|system]], the [[Starship/Legends|starship's]] [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] was critically damaged. Kenobi was able to locate a nearby planet without Trade Federation presence, [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where the group of fugitives would be able to purchase the repairs needed. Using Sabé as her proxy, Amidala agreed to the plan. The [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] that had made the speedy but temporary repairs that had allowed the ship to escape the blockade, [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], was commended by Sabé, who then "ordered" Amidala to clean him up.<ref name="tpm" />

Upon landing on the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] planet, Amidala herself set out for [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]], a nearby [[City/Legends|city]], with Jinn, the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], and R2-D2. While they were absent, Sabé received a message from [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Sio Bibble/Legends|Sio Bibble]], pleading her to contact him on Naboo. Kenobi cautioned against this, a warning Sabé heeded.<ref name="tpm" /> At any rate, she could not act without Amidala's authority, but Sabé still found the situation she was in to be highly taxing.<ref name="ff" /> While laying in wait, Sabé (still in the guise of Queen Amidala) was captured by [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]].<ref name="Star Wars: Obi-Wan video game">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref> Obi-Wan successfully rescued her, returning her safely to the ship while awaiting their companions' return. After several days, Amidala and Jinn were able to secure the parts, and the group set off for Coruscant.<ref name="tpm" />

Arriving at the [[Capital/Legends|capital]], Sabé again swapped identities with Amidala, allowing the real queen to deal with the critical [[Politics/Legends|political]] maneuvering that was sure to take place.<ref name="tpm" /> This allowed Sabé to take a break from her stressful role, although the respite was short-lived.<ref name="ff" /> Amidala was unsuccessful in her mission, and she decided to return to Naboo and take matters into her own hands.<ref name="tpm" />

===The Battle of Naboo===
{{Quote|Viceroy! Your occupation here has ended.|Sabé|<ref name="tpm" />}}
[[File:ArmedAndFabulous-TPM.jpg|thumb|right|210px|Sabé in the Battle of Naboo]]
On returning, Amidala and Sabé once more switched places due to the dangerous nature of the queen's plan. Queen Amidala had decided to make peace with the Gungans and persuade them to use their [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|army]] to aid in the liberation of Naboo. Sabé, in her guise as Amidala, went before [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]] and pleaded with him to join their cause. When Amidala saw that this was not working, she revealed her identity as a token of trust. Nass was initially taken aback by this move, then amused, and agreed to help the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]]. Sabé was to continue to assume the role of the queen in the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], although she would fight alongside Amidala herself.<ref name="tpm" /> During the battle, she met up with some members of the [[Naboo Underground]], and ordered them to provide a diversion as she and her compatriots made their way into the [[Theed Hangar/Legends|Theed Hangar]], so that the Naboo [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] would be able to launch in their [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|fighters]] without too much difficulty.<ref name="iotag">[[Star Wars: Invasion of Theed Adventure Game|''Star Wars: Invasion of Theed'' Adventure Game]]</ref>

As they battled their way through the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Theed Royal Palace]], Panaka came up with the idea of using [[Ascension gun/Legends|ascension guns]] to scale up the outside walls of the building. While Amidala and Panaka did this, Sabé continued to fight the long way through the enormous halls of the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|palace]], eventually reaching the [[Throne room (Theed Royal Palace)/Legends|throne room]]. When she got there, she found that Amidala and Panaka had been captured. Sabé, still in her royal attire, shouted out that the Federation's occupation had ended before destroying two [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] with her blaster. [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] Gunray, under the impression that she was the real queen, sent several other droids after her, but the distraction allowed Amidala to retrieve the weapons hidden in the arm of the [[Throne/Legends|throne]] itself. Amidala and Panaka destroyed the few remaining droid guards, sealed the throne room from the inside, and captured the Viceroy. Thanks to Sabé and Amidala's efforts, amongst those of many others, the battle was won, and Naboo was freed.<ref name="tpm" /> Following the battle, after the [[Funeral of Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|funeral of Jedi Master Qui-Gon Jinn]], who had been struck down in combat, Sabé again contacted elements of the Naboo Underground, and had them investigate [[Savor Kibbs]], the leader of a new renegade movement of [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and Gungans. The underground members eventually did battle with Kibbs in Naboo's [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]].<ref name="iotag" />

===Later career===
{{Dialogue|Skywalker|In fact, I'm pretty sure it's&hellip; Amidala's ''decoys''&mdash;Sabé&mdash;and Eritaé. ''[sic]''<nowiki />|Eirtaé|Actually, I'm Eritaé! ''[sic]''<nowiki></nowiki>|Sabé|And I'm Sabé!|attr=Anakin Skywalker is unable to distinguish between Sabé and Eirtaé|src=<ref name="In Triplicate" />}}
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] discovered that the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] had paid several outlaws on Coruscant to kidnap Amidala before a crucial speech in the Senate. In an effort to draw out the kidnappers, the Jedi hid Amidala in a safe location and allowed Sabé and Eirtaé to be [[Attempted kidnapping of Senator Amidala|captured]] instead. The Council then sent Anakin Skywalker&mdash;now a Jedi Knight and secretly Amidala's [[Wedding of Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala/Legends|husband]]&mdash;to rescue the senator; Skywalker was not aware of the exchange that had occurred. Skywalker successfully tracked down the kidnappers and subdued them. He released Amidala's decoys, but did not like the fact that he had not been told the truth about the Jedi Council's plans.<ref name="In Triplicate">{{TCWComicCite|6.3|In Triplicate}}</ref>

[[File:LilWinterNLeia-PLD.png|thumb|right|250px|Sabé tutored Leia and Winter in their youth and taught them skills they later used when they got older.]]
After the conclusion of the Clone Wars, Sabé continued to serve the eventual successor to Amidala in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]]&mdash;Jar Jar Binks. She remained suspicious of the circumstances of Amidala's [[Death/Legends|death]], joining forces with [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]], ally of the late queen. In her service to the [[House of Organa/Legends|House of Organa]], Sabé was employed as an envoy to establish resistance cells across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], gather and spread information, and handle the distribution of matériel to said rebel groups. Sabé also had the opportunity to interact with young [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and her friend [[Winter Celchu|Winter]]. Sabé tutored the girls; Organa in matters of court etiquette and diplomacy, and Winter in security and bodyguard tactics. These skills would later greatly serve both as agents of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="tfucg" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I never knew that a Jedi could be so rude.|Sabé|<ref name="tpmg">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref>}}
[[File:Sabe-SWE.png|thumb|left|200px|Sabé disguised as Queen Amidala in battle dress]]
Sabé was an extremely talented impersonator, fooling many in her act as Amidala. The ruse was not only successful due to her physical similarity to Amidala, but also to her skilled mimicry of Amidala's voice and mannerisms. Sabé was taught how to echo Amidala's gait by the queen herself.<ref name="ff" /> She was also a skilled combatant, fighting Federation droids at the Battle of Naboo. A crack shot with an [[ELG-3A blaster pistol/Legends|ELG-3A blaster pistol]], she managed to take off a droid's head with a single shot.<ref name="tpm" /> Although no harm ever befell her, Sabé was usually in great danger when disguised as the queen. She accepted this role dutifully, however.<ref name="vd" />

Sharp and calculating, Sabé became a close friend of Amidala during her time as a handmaiden, devising a set of hand signals that would enable communications between the two when playing their switched roles. Although she was adept in the role, Sabé would worry about ruining the deception with one slip of the tongue, and she found playing the part to be extremely stressful during the Invasion of Naboo, since she was effectively barred from making any actions whatsoever without Amidala's approval.<ref name="ff" /> In addition to her skills as a bodyguard, Sabé could speak [[Gungan (language)|Gunganese]], [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], [[Twi'leki/Legends|Twi'leki]], and could understand [[Shyriiwook/Legends|Shyriiwook]].<ref name="tfucg" />

==Behind the scenes==
Sabé was portrayed by [[Keira Knightley]] in [[George Lucas]]' [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].

The scenes with Sabé were filmed in and around the vicinity of [[Leavesden Studios]] in southern England in August 1997, two years before the official release of ''The Phantom Menace'' in 1999. At the time of filming, Knightley (born 26 March 1985) was twelve years old and ''The Phantom Menace'' became her second feature film, and her first "[[Wikipedia:Hollywood|Hollywood]]" motion picture.{{Fact}}

The role of Sabé was originally going to be filled by a [[Wikipedia:Stand-in|stand-in]], until casting director [[Robin Gurland]] came across Knightley, who bore a striking resemblance to [[Natalie Portman]], the actress playing the role of Padmé Amidala in the film. Knightley's role was kept quiet by ''The Phantom Menace''{{'s}} marketing department in order to heighten the surprise of there being a decoy queen when the film was released.

The queen's costumes were specifically designed to hide any height and shape differences between Knightley and Portman, so much in fact that even Portman's mother could not distinguish between the two on set.<ref name="ak">{{InsiderCite|75|Appearing Knightley (and the Women of Star Wars)|Appearing Knightley (and the Women of ''Star Wars'')}}</ref> Knightley can be seen out of character and standing in for Natalie Portman at a costume fitting segment in '<nowiki/>''The Beginning': Making Star Wars Episode I''', an hour long behind-the-scenes DVD bonus disc documentary which accompanied the DVD release of the film.

Keira Knightley is credited as "''Kiera Knightley''" in the end credits of ''The Phantom Menace, ''which is the usual and traditional Anglo-Irish spelling of the ''Kiera'' name''.''

In the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|video game adaptation]] of ''The Phantom Menace'', Obi-Wan Kenobi and Sabé, disguised as the queen, are separated from everyone else while fleeing Theed. Together, they venture through the war-torn city and find their way back to the group,<ref name="tpm" /><ref name="tpmg" /> although this does not correspond with events in the actual film.

Sabé was cut from the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', a [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]],<ref name="SWG">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=other|directory tree files}}</ref> prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> Sabé and four other Queen Amidala's handmaidens — [[Eirtaé/Legends|Eirtaé]], [[Rabé/Legends|Rabé]], [[Saché/Legends|Saché]] and [[Yané/Legends|Yané]] — were intended to be introduced in the game with the [[2005]] "[[W:c:swg:New Game Enhancements|New Game Enhancements]]." They would have been featured in a quest named "Helping the Handmaidens," included in the Naboo part of the so-called "[[W:c:swg:Legacy Quest|Legacy Quest]]," the longest questline in the game.<ref name="SWG" />
